subject: Short-window quota regrade & graceband proposal
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@cartistry.ai>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Contracts Ops <contracts@cartistry.ai>
Date: 2027-05-25T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Short runway request — surge for campaign launch

Hey Jordan / Markus,

Quick note — we have a time-boxed product marketing blast scheduled for June 2-4 that will triple request volume for a 48-hour window. Our infra team is asking for a pre-authorized bandwidth/throughput bump to avoid throttling and customer-impact.

Current committed throughput: 18k tokens/minute.
Expected peak: ~55k tokens/minute for ~48 hours.

Can Redwood provide a short-window quota regrade or a provisional burst band? We expect the traffic to be transient and are looking for a pricing approach that doesn't lock us into a permanent commit. Also need a note on how overrun true-ups will be invoiced.

If helpful, I attached our May usage snapshot.

Thanks,
Sam
Head of Platform — Cartistry AI
attachments: Cartistry_May_usage_snapshot.csv

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Sam Park <sam.park@cartistry.ai>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-25T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short runway request — surge for campaign launch

Sam — thanks for the heads-up and the usage export. High level: we can accommodate a short-window uplift with a provisional "graceband" that blends a temporary headroom rate and an overrun true-up to minimize sticker shock.

Proposed quick option (subject to approvals):
- Provisional burst window: up to 60k tokens/min for a 72-hour window (to cover your runway).
- Billing: any usage inside the window billed at a blended burst rate (25% premium over current paygo rate) up to the committed uplift; overrun beyond window billed as standard overrun true-up at 45% premium, with a cap on total uplift spend.
- Documentation: we provide an addendum for the window and a short amortized true-up if you prefer to smooth to next invoice.

I'll loop Markus and Grace to confirm approvals and legal wording. If that structure looks reasonable, we can produce the addendum and a DocuSign packet.

-Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-25T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Short runway request — surge for campaign launch

Jordan — thanks for the draft. Two internal asks before we send to Cartistry:
1) Can we tighten the blended premium to 20% (instead of 25%) if Cartistry agrees to a 30-day invoice net and provides a signed commitment to the 72-hour window? We want to keep commercial flexibility but reward a short contract commitment.
2) Add a one-time credit threshold: if the spike's cost-to-revenue exceeds X (we'll compute), offer a discretionary credit up to one invoice month as good will. This helps when customers have a marketing misfire.

Grace — can you run a quick estimate on expected token spend at 60k/min over 72 hours and draft the provisional addendum language (term, window, blended rate, overrun cap, credit condition)?

-Markus
VP, Sales Operations

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-25T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short runway request — surge for campaign launch

On calculations — 60k tokens/min * 60 min * 72 hrs = 259,200,000 tokens (peak-window theoretical). Given their May baseline, I estimate incremental tokens ~+230M for the window.

Draft addendum highlights I propose:
- Window: 2027-06-02T00:00:00Z through 2027-06-04T23:59:59Z (UTC)
- Blended burst rate: paygo_rate * 1.20 for usage up to the provisional uplift cap (cap = 260M tokens).
- Overrun true-up: usage above cap billed at paygo_rate * 1.45; customer may elect to amortize overrun on the following invoice over 1 month.
- One-time discretionary credit: up to 1x monthly committed invoice if incremental cost > 12% of projected incremental revenue (requires exec sign-off).
- Payment & terms: Net 30, DocuSign signature required.

I'll attach a worded addendum (provisional_burst_term_v2.docx) and a short pricing calc. Ready to send to Sam pending Markus approval.

-Grace
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: provisional_burst_term_v2.docx

From: Sam Park <sam.park@cartistry.ai>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: Contracts Ops <contracts@cartistry.ai>, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-26T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short runway request — surge for campaign launch

Jordan — that structure looks good and appreciated (the discretionary credit language is important). A couple of clarifying asks before we sign:
1) Can the provisional uplift cap be expressed in USD as well as tokens so we can map to our finance systems?
2) If we elect amortized true-up, can the repayment be settled over 2 invoices instead of 1? That smooths cashflow on our end.
3) Who should we expect to receive the DocuSign from and what is the turnaround SLA?

If those are fine, we'll sign quickly and provide a PO.

Thanks,
Sam

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Sam Park <sam.park@cartistry.ai>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-27T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short runway request — surge for campaign launch

Sam — good questions. Responses inline: 
1) We'll convert the cap to USD using your current paygo effective rate; preliminary estimate: 260M tokens ~= $7,800 (we'll include an exact USD cap in the addendum).
2) We can allow amortization over 2 invoices for this one-time short-window event (so long as you sign the addendum and provide a PO).
3) DocuSign will come from contracts@redwood.com (expect within 24 hours after you confirm). SLA for countersignature: we ask for 72 hours turnaround; we'll execute on our side within 24 hours of your signature.

I'll authorize sending the DocuSign packet once we have your confirmation on the two amortization and USD-cap items.

-Markus
VP, Sales Operations
attachments: docusign_proposal_burst.pdf
